In Claude Code it is also `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`. `<merlin-data>` is your Merlin data folder, `${user_config.data_dir}`; where that still reads as written, use the `data_root` value in `~/.merlin/instance.json`. Write both as absolute paths in every command you run, because a shell cannot expand either one.

# Task Management

One task list for your whole Merlin data folder: `<merlin-data>/TASKS.md`.
Tasks span every project, so they live in one file rather than scattered
per-project lists. A task engine that ships with Merlin does every write, so
two sessions can never overwrite each other's changes.

## When to use

Any request to add, complete, review, or reprioritize tasks.
Trigger phrases: "add a task", "remind me to", "what's on my plate",
"add to my task list", "finished X", "done with X", "what am I waiting on",
"reprioritize", "reorder my tasks", "triage my tasks".

## The list and the engine

- **The list:** `<merlin-data>/TASKS.md`. Never write a `TASKS.md` in the
  current folder and never create per-project task files. Merlin's setup
  creates the list; if it is missing, stop and tell the user to run
  `merlin:setup`.
- **The engine:** `<plugin-root>/lib/engine/triage-tasks/triage.py`, run with
  `python3`. Written `<engine>` below.
- **Never write a task line by hand, never pick an id, never strike a line
  through by hand.** The engine claims the id, writes the line and holds a
  lock on the file for the whole change.
- **If the engine refuses,** report its message in plain words and write
  nothing. A message about a missing setup step means: tell the user to run
  `merlin:setup`. Never work around a refusal by editing the file.
- Every write has a preview. Leave off `--commit` to see the change without
  writing it.

## Adding a task

```
python3 <engine>/triage.py add --list <merlin-data>/TASKS.md \
  --tag <Project> --text "**Short title.** longer description" \
  --section active --commit
```

1. **`--tag` is the bare project name, with no brackets.** Write
   `--tag Website`, never `--tag [Website]`. The engine adds the brackets.
   Use the project's folder name. A task that belongs to no project uses
   `--tag General`.
2. **`--text` is the body only,** with no checkbox and no id. Start it with a
   short bold title, then the description.
3. **`--section`** is `active`, `waiting` or `upcoming`.
4. Read the report: it names the id the engine gave the task and the line it
   wrote. Tell the user the id. They will refer to tasks by it ("close
   GE12").

The engine writes one line in this shape:

```markdown
- [ ] GE12 [Website] (2026-10-06) {P2}{waiting} **Short title.** longer description
```

Order is fixed: checkbox, id, `[Project]`, the date it was added, optional
tags, the bold title, then the description.

- **The title is a short command,** about 80 characters at most, readable with
  no other context. "Send the revised quote to the printer", not a paragraph.
- **Never end the title with a colon.** A bold span ending in `:` is read as a
  label, not a title.
- **Tags** go right before the title: priority `{P1}`, `{P2}` or `{P3}`, and
  status `{blocked}`, `{waiting}`, `{wip}` or `{next}`. Any other `{word}` is
  not a tag. Both are optional.
- **The date is the day the task was added,** never a due date. Due dates go
  in the description.

## Changing a task

Closing, annotating, retagging and moving all go through one command. Write
the changes to a small JSON file in a temporary folder (never inside the
Merlin data folder), then:

```
python3 <engine>/triage.py apply --file <merlin-data>/TASKS.md --ops <temp>/ops.json
```

Show the user the preview it prints, then run it again with `--commit`.

`ops.json` is a list. Each change names a task by its id and an action:

| Action | Fields | Does |
|---|---|---|
| `append` | `text` | adds text to the end of the task's line |
| `retag` | `priority` and/or `status` | swaps the `{P?}` and `{status}` tags |
| `close` | none | strikes the task through and moves it, with its notes, to Done |
| `keep` | none | resets the added date to today |
| `move` | `to` | moves it to `active`, `waiting` or `upcoming` |
| `update` | `text` | replaces the whole line (needs the full line, same id) |

```json
[{"tid": "GE12", "action": "append", "text": " -- Sent Tuesday, printer confirmed."},
 {"tid": "GE12", "action": "close"}]
```

Three rules the engine enforces:

- **One change per task per call,** except `append` then `close`, in that
  order, which is how a closing note reaches Done.
- **No line breaks in `text`.** A task is one line.
- **`update` keeps the id.** Text with a different id is refused.

Start `append` text with a space or ` -- `, because the engine joins it on
exactly as written.

**Only if the engine cannot run at all** (for example `python3` is missing):
say so, and offer a hand edit of the one line. Before writing, note the
file's size and modified time; re-check both just before writing; if either
changed, re-read and redo the edit; stop after two tries. Never invent an id
by hand.

## Sections

- **Active**: work the user will do, in priority order.
- **Waiting On**: blocked on someone else. Say who, what they owe, since
  when, and the target date if any. Move back to Active when unblocked.
- **Upcoming**: future or conditional tasks.
- **Done**: completed. Clear old items only when the user asks.

## Priority numbering

**Priority N** groupings are ordinal, not equal tiers. Priority 1 is the
single most urgent block of work this week; Priority 2 is next. Hard outside
deadlines (a client date, a contract, a meeting) always take Priority 1.

Keep P1 scarce. When a new `{P1}` would make more than about 10 open P1
tasks, warn the user and name the P1s that look like they could move down.

When a new planning cycle shifts priority, do NOT silently re-number. Ask
whether to re-order, or add the new tasks under a dated heading and point out
the conflict.

## When the user says "add a task"

1. Identify the project (ask if unclear). The tag is what groups the task.
2. Pick the section: hard deadline this week is `active` with `{P1}`, active
   work is `active`, blocked on someone is `waiting`, future is `upcoming`.
3. Run `add`. Report the id.
4. Several tasks from one meeting or planning session: add each one, and say
   which meeting they came from in each description.

## When the user says "done with X" / "completed X"

1. Find the task. An id ("close GE12") is exact. For a wording reference,
   find the single matching line first; if more than one matches, ask.
2. `apply` with `close`, after an `append` if there is a closing note.
3. Do NOT clear old Done items in the same change.

## When the user says "reprioritize" / "reorder"

1. Show the proposed new order and get a yes before writing.
2. Preserve tasks. Rearrange with `retag` and `move`; never delete.
3. Keep historical notes in place as context.

## When the user says "what am I waiting on"

Read the Waiting On section. For each item:
- Note how long it has been waiting (today minus its date).
- Flag items more than 3 days old as "may need a nudge".
- If a target date has passed, flag it as urgent.

## When extracting tasks from meetings or documents

Always confirm before adding. Offer each candidate as Active (with a
priority), Waiting On, Upcoming, or Skip (not actionable or already on the
list). Never add without a yes.

## When the user says "triage my tasks"

Triggers: "triage my tasks", "clean up my tasks", "review stale tasks",
"triage the backlog". Read `stale-triage.md` in this folder and follow it.
It walks every task older than 60 days, project by project, always with a
preview and a yes before anything is written.

## Related

- `stale-triage.md` in this folder: the clean-up mode.
